title: Homotopical quotient-section tower functors
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On a small skeleton of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], write $S_n=(A_n)_s$, $R=\lim_nS_n$, $\pi_n:R\to S_n$, and $\rho_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the category of flat-term K-flat $R$-complexes and all chain maps [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For $P\in\mathcal P$ set $P_n=P\otimes_RS_n$, $t_n=1\otimes\rho_n$, $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_n}g_n^*P_n$, and let $v_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ be induced by $G(t_n)$ and $\rho_n$, where $G=g^{-1}$ and $g_n^*M=GM\otimes_{GS_n}S_n$ uses the structure map $c_n:GS_n\to S_n$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ with its constant $\mathcal O_E$-action [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], and let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf Z_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_E))$ be the category of strict module towers [def-weil-inverse-system].

The constructions
$$D(P)=(\Gamma P_n,\Gamma t_n)_n,\qquad B(P)=(\Gamma C_n,\Gamma v_n)_n,$$
with maps $D(f)_n=\Gamma(f\otimes1)$ and $B(f)_n=\Gamma(g_n^*(f\otimes1))$, are additive functors $\mathcal P\to\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal A)$. The category $\mathcal A$ is abelian, with kernels, cokernels and cohomology computed levelwise. A chain map of its complexes is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when every level is one [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both functors send every quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal P$ to a quasi-isomorphism in $\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal A)$, without assuming any $S_n$ is flat over $R$.

For chain maps $f,f':P\to P'$ and a homotopy $h$ with $f-f'=d_{P'}h+hd_P$, the degree $-1$ maps with components $\Gamma(h\otimes1)$ and $\Gamma(g_n^*(h\otimes1))$ commute with every tower transition and are homotopies from $D(f')$ to $D(f)$ and from $B(f')$ to $B(f)$. Thus $QD,QB$, where $Q:\operatorname{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ is localization, factor through the homotopy category of $\mathcal P$.

For $N=[P]\in D(R)$, $D(P)$ represents levelwise exact sections of the entire coherent reduction tower $N_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi)$, transported to $D(\operatorname{Tow}_R(s))$ by restriction along the coefficient presentation isomorphisms $e_s$ and $\bar e_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison]; its $n$th evaluation is sections of $N\otimes_R^LS_n$, and its quotient augmentation is represented by $\Gamma(x\mapsto x\otimes1)$. The complex $B(P)$ represents sections of the finite pullback quotient tower on the same representative, with the displayed coefficient-induced transitions. These identifications retain the whole strict diagram, rather than only its separate derived evaluations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] to $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_E)$. This gives the asserted abelian category $\mathcal A$ and its levelwise kernels and cokernels. Images are kernels of cokernels, so $H^i(T)_n=\ker(d^i_n)/\operatorname{im}(d^{i-1}_n)=H^i(T_n)$ for a tower complex $T$. A map of towers is invertible exactly when all its components are: the inverses commute with transitions by multiplying its naturality squares by these inverses. Applying this to $H^i(f)$ and using the definition of quasi-isomorphism proves the levelwise criterion. In Lean use the functor-category abelian instances, the homology isomorphism of exact evaluation on short complexes, whiskered by the short-complex functor, and HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_iff_evaluation.

proof.text: First work before sections. By the sheaf tensor definition, $t_n^i$ sends $x\otimes a$ to $x\otimes\rho_n(a)$, and $f_n^i=f^i\otimes1$ sends it to $f^i(x)\otimes a$. Thus $t_n^{P\prime}f_{n+1}=f_nt_n^P$: both send $x\otimes a$ to $f(x)\otimes\rho_n(a)$. The same calculation with $f=d_P$ gives a complex of strict towers. Identity, composition and addition of maps hold on pure tensors. These are equalities of the presheaf tensor maps, hence of their sheafifications. Restriction along $\pi_n$ gives $R$-linear transitions because $\rho_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$. Additive sections, with scalars restricted along the constant map $\mathcal O_E\to\Gamma(s,R)$, give precisely $D(P)$ and $D(f)$. This proves the asserted additive functor $D$. Reuse the canonical unrestrictedIntegralComplexFunctor and unrestrictedIntegralTransition of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]; their strict diagram is already constructed. Additivity follows degreewise and levelwise from the additive quotient, restriction and sections functors.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism f between good representatives, apply the K-flat quasi-isomorphism invariance in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to each actual quotient projection. The existing finiteReduction_quasiIso proof in [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] is this specialization. The specified constant-coefficient finite pullback is exact by [lem-pur-coefficient-pullback-exact], so it preserves this quasi-isomorphism. Exact scalar restriction and exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] preserve it as well. Apply Step 1 to assemble these levelwise results into quasi-isomorphisms of both entire tower complexes. No flatness of a quotient over the completed ring is used.

source.place: Tag 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side; exact point sections and scalar transport

proof.text: Write $h^i:P^i\to P\prime^{i-1}$ for the given homotopy. The transition calculation of Step 2 applies to each $h^i$, without using a chain-map identity, and gives $t_n^{P\prime}(h^i\otimes1)=(h^i\otimes1)t_n^P$. The calculation of Step 3 likewise applies to $G(h^i\otimes1)$ and the coefficient-induced transitions. Thus, after sections, these degree $-1$ maps are morphisms of towers. Tensor, inverse image, scalar extension and sections are additive and respect composition. Applying them to $f^i-f\prime^i=d_{P\prime}^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_P^i$ gives, in $\mathcal A$, $D(f)-D(f\prime)=dD(h)+D(h)d$ and $B(f)-B(f\prime)=dB(h)+B(h)d$. These are the asserted homotopies with the stated direction and components. For the actual Lean transitions, first identify unrestrictedIntegralTransition with the termwise unrestrictedModuleStep by its tensor-normalized uniqueness. Its naturality applies to every h(i,j), with no chain-map requirement. Identify integralOperationsPullbackTransition with its constructed candidate by its generator-normalized uniqueness; the finite pullback mate naturality gives the corresponding square for every h(i,j). NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles these adjacent squares into genuine tower maps. The zero and homotopy equations are the level additive functors mapHomotopy equations, checked by natural-transformation extensionality.

The localization $Q$ factors through the homotopy category by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By Step 5, replacing a chain map in $\mathcal P$ by a homotopic map replaces its image under either $D$ or $B$ by a homotopic map. Hence $QD$ and $QB$ assign equal morphisms to equivalent chain maps and define functors on the quotient of $\mathcal P$ by chain homotopy. Their identity and composition laws follow from those already proved for $D$ and $B$. Explicitly use DerivedCategory.Q_map_eq_of_homotopy and CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift with its canonical lift.isLift isomorphism for each functor.

Let $F(P)$ be the strict reduction tower defined in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $N=[P]$, that definition computes $N_\bullet$ by this very tower on one K-flat representative, not by separately chosen representatives at different levels. The datum applies: $\mathcal O_E$ is Noetherian, $\mathcal O_E/\varpi$ is a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, hence torsion, and each $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ is finite and perfect, resolved by $0\to\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}\mathcal O_E\to0$. Its ring sheaves are its Cont-presentations $L_n$ of $\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ and $B_s=\varprojlim_nL_n$, not $S_n$ and $R$; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison] gives ring-sheaf isomorphisms $e_s:B_s\to R$ and $\bar e_n:L_n\to S_n$ with $\pi_ne_s=\bar e_n\pi_n^{B}$, compatible with the quotient transitions, and exact inverse restriction equivalences. Restricting $P$ along $e_s$ gives a flat-term K-flat $B_s$-complex $P^\flat$, since tensoring with a transported acyclic complex gives the same underlying complex. The balanced maps $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes\bar e_n(a)$, well defined because $\pi_ne_s=\bar e_n\pi_n^B$ and inverse to $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\bar e_n^{-1}(b)$, identify $F(P^\flat)_n$ with $P\otimes_RS_n$ restricted along $\bar e_n$, compatibly with differentials and with the transitions $1\otimes q_{n+1,n}$ and $t_n$ since $\rho_n\bar e_{n+1}=\bar e_nq_{n+1,n}$. So the transported coherent tower of $N$ is represented by the strict tower $F(P)_n=P\otimes_RS_n$ with transitions $t_n$. Define sections on $R$-module towers degreewise and levelwise, with constant $\mathcal O_E$-scalars. It is exact: kernels and cokernels are levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], and sections at each level are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Its derived functor is therefore computed on every complex by the termwise construction [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Applied to $F(P)$ it is exactly $D(P)$, including every transition. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies each evaluation with sections of $N\otimes_R^LS_n$. The maps $a_n(x)=x\otimes1$ commute with differentials and satisfy $t_na_{n+1}=a_n$, since $\rho_n(1)=1$; sections therefore give the stated strict quotient augmentation. Finally exactness of $g_n^*$ from Step 4 means the finite pullback of this representative is computed by $g_n^*P_n$. Step 3 constructs precisely its coefficient-induced transitions, so its section complex is $B(P)$. All identifications are made on these complexes of towers themselves and thus in their derived categories; none infers an identification of coherent diagrams from evaluations alone. The strict quotient augmentation is checked before localization using unrestrictedTowerUnit_condition and the tensor-normalized transition, then assembled with NatTrans.ofOpSequence and whiskered by sections. Its finite-evaluation corollary uses unrestrictedTowerResolutionIso of [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined] on the identity K-flat resolution of P, followed by the canonical exact-restriction and sections localization factorization isomorphisms. Apply [lem-trf-point-quotient-tower-strict-comparison] for the normalized isomorphism of complexes of whole towers, and [lem-trf-pbc-iso-restriction-kflat] for the coefficient-transported K-flat representative. The published completedReductionTower_properties makes the universal counit invertible on this representative. The completed-tower image of the restriction localization factor, this counit, the tower-restriction localization factor, Q(r), and the sections localization factor are all invertible. Compose the corresponding canonical factor isomorphisms, using the published counit-isomorphism lemma; the resulting gamma.hom is definitionally the prescribed literal composite. The ordinary strict comparison is the remaining subproblem, before sections and localization. The completed assembly is the extracted coherentSource theorem of [lem-trf-point-quotient-tower-coherent-source], publicly re-exported by the item. The unchanged tower definitions are [def-trf-point-quotient-tower-data].
